title: Missing Admission Control / Load Shedding under Overload
pattern: An incoming request processing loop that unconditionally accepts, queues, and attempts to execute every incoming request without checking current server load, queue depth limits, or system capacity thresholds.
why_bad: When offered load exceeds processing capacity, the length of the processing queue grows linearly, which increases latency and wastes memory [53, 583]. Without load shedding or admission control, the completion time for all requests degrades rapidly, eventually crashing the process from memory exhaustion or leading to a system-wide hang as clients time out [583]. A resilient system must reject excess requests ("TooBusy") quickly [583].
detection: Identify request-processing pathways that do not track queue depths, active request counts, or load indicators, and lack fail-fast rejection blocks.
fix: Implement active admission control by measuring queue depths or processing times, rejecting excess traffic with a "Too Busy" code to preserve capacity for existing transactions [583].
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 29 / passage [583]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 8 / passage [46].
